name: WealthStrat: Institutional Leverage Engine
tag: See your capital stack, investor pitch structure and K-1 distribution waterfall in one place.

scenarios.title: Build a capital stack
scenarios.ask: Fund a ${cost} project with {senior} senior debt and {mezz} mezzanine. Show the rest as equity.
steps: Stack builder
Senior debt ${=round(cost * senior / 100)} and mezzanine ${=round(cost * mezz / 100)}.
Equity
Equity fills the rest: ${=round(cost * (100 - senior - mezz) / 100)}.
Split
Sponsor puts in {gp} of equity, investors the other {=100 - gp}%.
Chart
Drew the stack from first-paid to last-paid so investors see their position.
followups: Senior debt, then mezzanine, then equity. That order is why debt usually costs less than equity.
It depends on the asset and lender. Higher leverage can raise equity returns and also raises the risk of loss if values fall. The engine runs downside cases for this.

scenarios.title: Run a distribution waterfall
scenarios.ask: We have ${cash} to distribute. Investors put in ${lpcap} with a {pref} preferred return, then a {split} split.
steps: Tier 1
Investors receive the {pref} preferred return first: ${=round(min(cash, lpcap * pref / 100))}.
Tier 2
Remaining cash: ${=round(max(0, cash - lpcap * pref / 100))}, split {split} between investors and sponsor.
Totals
Added each party's share across tiers.
K-1 prep
Mapped each party's distributions to the K-1 schedule for the accountant.

result.title: Waterfall (one year, simplified)
rows: ${=round(min(cash, lpcap * pref / 100) + max(0, cash - lpcap * pref / 100) * split)}
{=round((min(cash, lpcap * pref / 100) + max(0, cash - lpcap * pref / 100) * split) / lpcap * 100, 1)}%
Simplified model, no catch-up or return of capital tier

followups: Some deals let the sponsor receive a larger share right after the preferred return until it reaches its target split. You can switch a catch-up tier on in the full model.
Does this replace the operating agreement?
No. The waterfall must follow your operating agreement exactly. The engine shows it visually so investors can follow it.

scenarios.title: Structure an investor pitch
scenarios.ask: Outline a pitch to raise ${raise} from investors with a minimum check of ${minimum}.
steps: Outline agent
Built a 10-slide outline: thesis, market, deal, capital stack, waterfall, team, risks, timeline, terms, next steps.
Math agent
At a ${minimum} minimum, the raise needs at most {=ceil(raise / minimum)} investors.
Risk writer
Drafted a plain-language risks slide covering leverage, market and execution.
Review list
Flagged items for securities counsel before anything goes to investors.
followups: Securities rules can limit how many and what kind of investors you take, and each investor adds reporting work. Counsel should confirm which exemption you use.
It builds the outline and charts. You or your designer finish the deck.
